summary.title: Imaginative Perception Tokens Enhance Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Language Models

setting_and_object.category: Method (training supervision) plus accompanying task suite/datasets

details: Spatial questions often hinge on structure that is not observable in the input (an unseen viewpoint, an occluded path, a scene spread across partial views), so intermediate representations that merely refine visible structure (depth, boxes, visual thoughts) do not help.
Serializing viewpoint transformations and cross-view correspondences into textual chain-of-thought is a modality mismatch.

Imaginative Perception Tokens (IPT): supervising a unified understanding+generation VLM to first generate an image of what would be perceived under an alternative, unobserved spatial configuration (novel viewpoint, midpoint sideview, aggregated bird's-eye map), then condition the textual answer on that generated percept.

Trained with a joint flow-matching loss on the imagined-image latent plus a language-modeling loss on the answer; at inference the model can either generate and re-encode the imagination or answer directly.

Accompanying contribution: three imaginative-perception tasks (Perspective Taking, Path Tracing, Multiview Counting), each with ~20K training examples paired with ground-truth intermediate imaginations and human-filtered benchmarks.

Perspective Taking: first-person view with a red 'X' target position; answer distance-change or left/right after moving and turning 90 degrees; GT imagination = rendered novel-viewpoint image. 20,531 AI2-THOR train examples (mixed variant 55,529 with Habitat/HM3D and real Visual Spatial Tuning camera-motion data); benchmarks of 238 (AI2-THOR) and 300 (Habitat) human-verified items; accuracy averaged over six balanced sub-categories.

Path Tracing: top-down map with numbered waypoints (variants EgoDir / Path / PathArr); answer which object is visible on a given side at midpoint M1; GT imagination = rendered sideview at M1. 11,204 synthetic AI2-THOR/ProcTHOR examples plus a 332-question human-verified Matterport3D real benchmark; TIFA-style GPT-4.1 filtering removes items answerable from the top-down/egocentric views alone.

Multiview Counting: four (or 5-8 for ScanNet++) egocentric frames, 4-choice count MCQ with +/-1,2 distractors; GT imagination = top-down BEV map. 17,079 synthetic train examples (mixed 19,499 with MessyTable and ScanNet++ real data); 260-sample human-verified benchmark.
All main models trained on the AI2-THOR subset only for controlled comparison.
Backbone BAGEL-7B-MoT (Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts; SigLIP2 ViT understanding tokens plus FLUX VAE generation tokens in a shared context).
AdamW lr 1e-5, 2,000 warmup steps, EMA 0.9999, FSDP bf16 on 8 A100-80GB; VAE frozen, LLM/ViT/connector fine-tuned; loss weights lambda_fm = lambda_lm = 1.0.
Inference: 50 diffusion steps, text CFG 4.0, image CFG 2.0, generated images 1024x1024; answers parsed from <answer> tags.

Variants: BAGEL base (zero-shot), label-only fine-tuning, + Text CoT (traces written by GPT-5.1 from simulator ground-truth metadata), + IPT, + Mixed Training (50% IPT prompts / 50% answer-only prompts, switchable via system prompt).
Baselines: GPT-5, GPT-5.2, Gemini 2.5/3 Flash, InternVL3.5-8B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B; unified models Janus-Pro-7B and Chameleon-7B, all zero-shot.
IPT latent resolution ablation (Latent-4 = 64x64 up to Latent-64 = 1024x1024).
Inference mode ablation: generate imagination vs. answer-only vs. oracle ground-truth imagination injected.
Transfer to external benchmarks: SAT perspective-taking subset, MessyTable counting, plus ScanNet, MindCube, All-Angles-Bench with an answer-only MVC-fine-tuned model.
Appendix: discrete-token IPT with VQGAN codebooks appended to Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B vocabulary, plus grayscale and depth intermediate targets.

key_findings.finding: Imaginative image supervision improves spatial reasoning over answer-only fine-tuning, especially for cross-environment and multiview settings.
key_findings.evidence: On Multiview Counting IPT reaches 67.3% vs 63.9% label-only and 62.3% Text CoT; on Habitat Perspective Taking IPT gets 87.0% vs 82.0% label-only, with Mixed Training at 87.7%; on real-world Path Tracing IPT 57.5% vs 54.7% label-only, and Mixed Training is best on both synthetic (66.7%) and real (58.6%) PT splits.

key_findings.finding: The benefit comes from the training signal rather than from generating an image at test time; answer-only inference often beats explicitly generating the imagination.
key_findings.evidence: On Path Tracing an IPT-trained model scores 61.1% in answer-only mode vs 50.4% when generating the imagination, matching GPT-5's 61.1%; IPT answer-only also beats Text CoT answer-only by 5.3 points (61.1% vs 55.8%).

key_findings.finding: Textual chain-of-thought supervision actively hurts on these spatial tasks, falling below plain answer-only fine-tuning.
key_findings.evidence: Text CoT reaches 83.1% vs 97.5% label-only on AI2-THOR PET and 49.7% vs 65.7% on PT, and is also below IPT on MVC (62.3% vs 67.3%) and PET (83.1% vs 96.8%).

key_findings.finding: Imagination fidelity is the dominant bottleneck for the hardest task, and higher-resolution latents produce better imaginations and higher accuracy.
key_findings.evidence: Substituting ground-truth imaginations raises PT from 50.4% to 86.7% (+36.3) and MVC from 63.1% to 67.3%, while PET is already saturated (96.8% generated vs 96.7% GT); raising latent resolution from Latent-4 to Latent-64 improves PET 87.4%->96.8% and MVC 53.5%->63.1%, though Habitat PET peaks at Latent-32 (87.0%) and drops to 83.3% at Latent-64.

key_findings.finding: Training on these simulator-based imagination tasks yields spatial representations that transfer to unrelated external spatial benchmarks.
key_findings.evidence: Mixed Training reaches 63.6% on SAT perspective-taking (base 34.9%, label-only 59.1%) and 37.0% on MessyTable (base 29.0%); an MVC answer-only fine-tune improves ScanNet 40.5%->52.0%, MindCube 39.5%->47.5%, All-Angles 40.0%->50.0%.
